output.question: Has Ford announced layoffs?
output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, I found no new, company-wide layoff announcement from Ford Motor Co. this fall with a specific headcount. Ford's 10-Q filings say it expects $500 million to $1 billion of 2026 restructuring charges, mostly for employee separations, with Europe the main focus. Some of these plans still have to be negotiated with works councils or unions, and Ford has not put a number on the job cuts. The largest confirmed 2026 cut was at BlueOval SK, Ford's battery joint venture, not Ford itself. Its Glendale, Kentucky battery plant laid off about 1,500–1,600 workers from February 14, 2026 so the plant could be retooled for energy-storage batteries. A May 2026 CNBC report described Ford's salaried cuts as gradual: about 5,300 fewer salaried staff than at the 2020 peak, leaving roughly 30,700.

key_facts.fact: Ford's 10-K and 10-Q filings guide to $500 million–$1 billion of total 2026 charges for actions already started, 'primarily attributable to employee separations'. Some plans are still subject to works council or union negotiations, and no headcount is given.
Ford booked $360M of European restructuring special items in H1 2026, compared with $50M in H1 2025.

A BlueOval SK (Ford/SK On joint venture) WARN notice for Glendale, KY was reported at 1,218 hourly and 300 salaried workers. Layoffs began February 14, 2026, and the plant is being retooled to reopen in 2027 with about 2,100 jobs.
Ford has cut about 5,300 salaried workers from its 2020 peak, to about 30,700 white-collar employees in 2025.
SK-related battery sites filed WARN notices in March 2026: SK Battery America in Commerce, GA (958 workers) and BlueOval SK in Haywood County, TN (150 workers), both effective May 6, 2026.

passages.quote: total charges in 2026 that range between $500 million and $1 billion related to such actions ... primarily attributable to employee separations
some charges are related to plans that are subject to negotiations with a works council, union, or other social partner
From its salaried employment peak in 2020, Ford has scaled back by roughly 5,300 workers to reach about 30,700 white-collar employees last year.

caveats: I could not open Note 14 of the Q3 2026 10-Q (filed about October 28, 2026; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000037996/000003799626000191/f-20260930.htm) because the fetch was truncated. A search summary says it repeats the $500M–$1B 2026 guidance and shows a $916M separation reserve at September 30, 2026, but I did not read this myself.
The Glendale, Georgia and Tennessee cuts were made by BlueOval SK or SK On entities, which are Ford joint ventures or partners, not Ford Motor Co. itself.
Analyst estimates of 8,000–11,000 Ford job losses in 2026 are projections that blogs keep repeating. Ford has not confirmed them.
A November 10, 2026 news item about a 'Ford' approving travel on the day of layoffs is about the Jacksonville Transportation Authority's former CEO, not Ford Motor.
Fox 2 Detroit and others report that Ford rehired about 300–350 engineers after earlier cuts. I did not verify this.
I found no Ford newsroom statement dated November 2026. An announcement made in the last few days could be missing from these results.
